snippet.title: Trump and Xi agree on ending Iran nuclear threat, need to open Strait of Hormuz
snippet.description:

Staying in Beijing, Presidents Trump and Xi appear to have found common ground on Iran, signaling shared opposition to Tehran acquiring nuclear weapons and a mutual desire to bring the ongoing conflict to an end.
Cho Young-eun reports.

As the U.S.-China summit concluded on Friday, Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping appeared to find common ground on Iran, agreeing that Tehran must not obtain a nuclear weapon and that the Strait of Hormuz should be kept open amid escalating regional conflict.
President Trump said both leaders shared similar views on ending the conflict involving Iran, and preventing further instability in the Middle East.

"We did discuss Iran. We feel very similar on Iran. We want that to end. We don’t want them to have a nuclear weapon. We want the Straits open."

President Trump later told Fox News that Xi also stated China would not provide military equipment to Iran, a move Trump described as "a big statement."
Earlier, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington hoped Beijing would play a more active diplomatic role in resolving the crisis because it relies heavily on energy shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

China’s foreign ministry called again on Friday for a ceasefire and urged that the Strait of Hormuz be reopened "as soon as possible."
The issue is particularly significant for China, with nearly half of its crude oil imports passing through the strategic waterway.
Still, many in Beijing reportedly view the Iran crisis as outside China’s direct responsibility, raising questions over how far Xi is willing to cooperate with Washington on the issue.
Meanwhile, tensions around the strait continued to escalate as one ship anchored near the United Arab Emirates was seized and taken toward Iran on Thursday, while another cargo vessel near Oman sank following an attack.

Although no group immediately claimed responsibility, the incidents came as Iranian officials reiterated Tehran’s authority over the waterway and asserted its right to seize oil tankers linked to the United States.

Cho Young-eun, Arirang News.

snippet.description:

The two-day official candidate registration for the local elections ended today at 6 PM with last-minute variables, including candidate mergers appearing between the ruling Democratic Party and the Progressive Party in the city of Ulsan. 
Our political correspondent Ahn Sung-jin has the details.

Ahead of the June 3rd local elections, official candidate registration has wrapped up, setting the stage for intensified campaigning in several key battlegrounds across the country. 
The National Election Commission accepted registrations over two days ---May 14th and 15th ---and officials are expected to finalize ballot numbers for candidates based on parliamentary representation before official ballot printing on the 18th.
Candidate disclosures, including assets, criminal records, and tax payments, will be made public through the NEC election information system. 

Attention has centered on the southeastern city of Ulsan, where the ruling Democratic Party and the Progressive Party reached a last-minute agreement to unify their candidacies in a bid to challenge their conservative rival. 
Under the agreement, the two parties will select a single candidate for the mayor of Ulsan through public opinion polling. 
They also agreed to coordinate candidacies in five district-level county chief races as some candidates withdraw in favor of their allies, while others enter primary-style races to determine a unified nominee. 
This merger is expected to reshape the mayoral race in a traditionally conservative region, as recent opinion polls showed strong support for conservative candidates. 

The cooperation extends beyond Ulsan. 
The two parties also agreed to field a single candidate in the mayoral race for Yeonje-gu District in the southern port city of Busan. 
Similar consolidation deals have already emerged in several races nationwide, including district heads in Seoul, Daejeon, and Gyeongsangnam-do Province. 
Political parties across the spectrum are expected to continue negotiations ahead of two critical deadlines: candidates who withdraw by May 17th will have "withdrawn" marked beside their names on election day ballots, while those stepping down by the 28th, one day before early voting, will be identified as "withdrawn" on early voting ballots. 

The local elections are to elect 16 mayors and provincial governors, 227 county chiefs, more than 3,900 local council members, and 16 education superintendents, alongside 14 parliamentary seats through by-elections. 

Ahn Sung-jin, Arirang News.

South Korea's benchmark KOSPI broke past the eight thousand mark for the first time during early trade on this Friday before closing its session lower on profit-taking.
Our economics correspondent Kim Jun-hong  has more.

Korea's benchmark KOSPI passed above the 8-thousand mark for the first time ever during trading on Friday.
 The index closed at 7-thousand-4-hundred-93-point18, down 6.12 percent from the previous session. 
 The move above 8-thousand came roughly ten minutes after the opening bell, just seven trading days after first breaking through the 7-thousand mark.
Yet sharp swings dominated trading throughout the day.
 The index seesawed between gains and losses before falling as much as seven percent from the previous session during trading, triggering a sell-side sidecar at one point.

Unlike the previous rally led by the country's chip giants, Friday's gains were powered by a wider group of market heavyweights.
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix both ended lower, while shares of LG Electronics and Hyundai Motor moved higher.
All of the gainers are part of the broader AI value chain, including sectors tied to memory chips, energy, and semiconductor materials.

"One of Friday's key themes was growing attention to LG Group's shift toward AI-focused businesses, which helped lift related stocks. More broadly, Korea’s market continues to see strong rallies in companies tied to the wider AI ecosystem."


During Friday's session, foreign investors continued to take profits from major chipmakers.
Given the outsized influence those semiconductor heavyweights have on the benchmark index, the broader market was also dragged lower by the selling pressure.
With the record-breaking rally largely driven by the country's chip giants riding the semiconductor super cycle, overheating concerns and the risk of heightened volatility continue to fuel caution in the market.

"Volatility in Korea's stock market has surged sharply. Historically, the gap between intraday highs and lows averaged around 1.4 percent, but recent swings have widened to 3 to 4 percent. That marks the third-highest level since the global financial crisis and the pandemic."


"Brokerages at home and abroad are raising their KOSPI targets as the rally continues, with some even talking about the index reaching 10-thousand. But with market volatility, attention is now on whether the rally will cool off or move higher.

Kim Jun-hong, Arirang News."

snippet.description:

Culture Minister Chae Hwi-young  was in the city of Miryang  in Korea's Gyeongsangnam-do Province to learn firsthand about the impact of government programs to breathe new life into smaller cities through culture and tourism.
Our culture correspondent Park Kun-woo  was there.

Students sing and dance passionately during a performance inspired by "Miryang Arirang," a traditional folk song unique to the region.
In Miryang, a southeastern city grappling with population decline, these young students are also taking part in efforts to promote their hometown through local cultural performances.
This has been a big help, as the city's been designated as a "culture city" ---part of a governmental program aimed at revitalizing such regions through local cultural content.


"I feel like I should have visited much earlier. Local culture seems to be growing stronger on the foundations we've worked on. We'll continue listening to what support is needed and do our best moving forward."

During a two-day visit to the city, Culture Minister Chae Hwi-young also met with local residents to hear firsthand about the challenges they face.
Miryang has been one of the pioneer cities to apply the government-backed "half-cost travel" program, and officials say they've witnessed a boost in visitor numbers.
But local merchants are asking for more support.


"I hope the program can be promoted earlier and backed with a larger budget so more people can benefit from it. If the half-price travel program becomes more active, it will greatly help revitalize the regional economy."

Amid the shrinking population, people relocating to the countryside and setting up their own businesses is also becoming more noticeable in the city.
But some say support programs are sometimes unreachable.


"I'm in my 40s, and when it comes to support programs or opportunities to participate, I've become too old to qualify. In agriculture, people are considered young enough to earn support until 50, so I hope there can be broader support for people like us as well."


"It's inspiring to see the younger generation's efforts to rediscover strengths in places once weakened, and these efforts deserve continued support. More successful cases need to emerge so that others will also be inspired to follow the path."


"With more support from the culture ministry and continued efforts to further develop the region’s cultural content, the area is now looking to attract more visitors and boost regional growth.
Park Kun-woo, Arirang News, Miryang."

The Lee administration's pragmatic diplomacy includes advancing bilateral interests with partners in the Global South.
This being said my colleague Oh Soo-young  reached out to a senior official at the Foreign Ministry here for a better understanding of these related efforts.
Do take a listen.

People and partnerships are at the heart of Seoul’s expanding diplomatic reach.
Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Lim Sang-woo is playing an active role in deepening ties across the Global South, while strengthening support for Koreans abroad.
Since taking office last December, Kenya and Madagascar were among his first overseas trips, ahead of a ministerial meeting involving 54 African countries next month.

“This is also in the context of our diplomacy that focuses more on strengthening our relationship with the Global South and of course in Africa is an integral part of the Global South.”

Global South outreach featured in President Lee Jae Myung’s summit last month with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, marking the first Korean state visit to India in eight years.
One crucial agreement supports Korean SMEs investing in India, an initiative Lim personally worked on during his posting in New Delhi.
His diplomacy went beyond official meetings.
From creating viral videos to volunteering as a guide at India’s National Museum, a first for a foreign diplomat.
His outreach now informs his role overseeing KOREAZ, the foreign ministry’s public diplomacy platform,.. supported by 20 Koreans and 20 foreign nationals representing 18 countries.

“We are committed to running this channel not as just a platform to showcase Korean culture but a channel where genuine dialogue takes place with our friends from all over the world."

But as Korea’s global reach expands, so does the responsibility of protecting some seven million overseas nationals, amid risks from armed conflict and natural disasters, to transnational crime.

“Our guiding principle has been to provide Koreans security protection that they would expect to have at home.
So in that way Koreans wherever they are in the world can feel secure and feel safe having this assurance that the government will be there to provide assistance if needed.”

Lim last week travelled to Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, where Seoul is working with local authorities to tackle online scam operations involving Koreans.

“The most critical tool we can use to combat transnational crime is real-time intelligence. There has to be a real-time sharing of intelligence amongst the law enforcement authorities, and there has to be swift and decisive action based on those real time intelligence.”

From serving in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and as Korea’s first resident ambassador to Madagascar, Lim has built relationships from the ground up, 
and responded to consular crises in times of conflict and pandemic.
Oh Soo-young, Arirang News.

South Korea's export prices surged in April, with the export price index marking 187-point-four-zero, up 7-point-1 percent from the previous month.

Central bank data also shows import prices fell 2-point-3 percent on-month in April, marking the first on-month drop in 10 months.

However, prolonged geopolitical tensions in the region continue to pose upward risks for future raw material supplies.
Prices of raw materials fell 9-point-7 percent in April from a month earlier, while intermediate goods rose 2-point-1 percent.
Despite these uncertainties, the country's net barter terms of trade index improved, jumping 14-point-3 percent on-year.
The South Korean economy continues its recovery trend on the back of strong semiconductor exports, and domestic consumption has maintained its recovery. 
However, as the Middle East conflict remains ongoing, consumer sentiment has weakened while rising global oil prices are intensifying financial burdens on the people.

Korea's economy is seeing a massive boost, driven largely by a historic boom in the technology sector. 
Not only have information and communication technology exports reached an all-time high, but this semiconductor supercycle is also helping to rapidly improve the government's fiscal health. 
Joining us in the studio to break down these numbers and the broader implications is our Business and Economy correspondent Kim Do-yeon. Welcome.

Good to be here.

Let's start with the export data. April was a milestone month for the tech sector. Walk us through the latest figures.

That's right ICT exports logged their highest growth rate in history last month. 
Export volume reached 42.71 billion U.S. dollars, which is a 125.9 percent surge compared to the same month last year. 
This marks the first time ICT exports have surpassed the 40-billion-dollar mark for two consecutive months. 
The semiconductor sector is doing the heavy lifting, skyrocketing 173.3 percent on-year.
The global tech industry is racing to build artificial intelligence infrastructure, creating a severe bottleneck for high-performance memory chips. 
Here is what one industry expert had to say about this momentum.

"The reason our ICT exports are hitting all-time highs right now is the supply shortage in memory chip exports, which is driving prices incredibly high. Because of this, it's very likely we will break records again next month."

And we are already seeing this spill over into the computer and peripheral devices sector, which saw a staggering 430 percent export increase, heavily influenced by the AI-driven demand for solid-state drives.

It is interesting how this industrial boom is translating directly into the national treasury. The government's first-quarter fiscal data released today shows a significantly narrowed deficit.

According to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the managed fiscal balance—which indicates the government's actual fiscal state—posted a deficit of 39.6 trillion won in the first quarter. 
While still a deficit, this is an improvement of 21.7 trillion won compared to a year ago, making it the narrowest first-quarter deficit in six years.
This was driven by a massive increase in total revenue, which reached 188.8 trillion won. 
A closer look reveals that income tax revenue rose by 4.7 trillion won, fueled directly by increased performance bonuses for employees at semiconductor giants like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix along with other industries and government policies. 
But bonuses are important because a big portion of the bonuses are taxed. 
However, experts point out that relying so heavily on just one sector creates a dangerous optical illusion for the broader economy. Take a listen.

"Because of companies in a small number of industries, it looks like our economy is doing well and recovering, but in some ways, this is a severe polarization. The industries that are struggling are simply continuing to struggle. So, while we can't say it's strictly just semiconductors, it is true that this is limited to a few industries and a few companies."

Essentially, while the headline numbers and government coffers look phenomenal thanks to chips, other sectors of the domestic economy are still struggling, meaning the wealth is not trickling down evenly.

You mentioned the performance bonuses at semiconductor companies boosting national tax revenues. But ironically, those same bonuses are currently the source of a major dispute within Samsung Electronics. What is the latest on the strike concerns?

The situation at Samsung is reaching a critical point as the gap between labor and management remains wide.
The union is specifically demanding that the company institutionalize a fixed performance bonus of 15 percent of its operating profit for the semiconductor division. 
They are also calling for the removal of the current cap on bonuses, which is currently set at 50 percent of an employee's annual salary.

President Trump said both leaders shared similar views on ending the conflict involving Iran, and preventing further instability in the Middle East.

"We did discuss Iran. We feel very similar on Iran. We want that to end. We don’t want them to have a nuclear weapon. We want the Straits open."

President Trump later told Fox News that Xi also stated China would not provide military equipment to Iran, a move Trump described as "a big statement."
Earlier, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington hoped Beijing would play a more active diplomatic role in resolving the crisis because it relies heavily on energy shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

China’s foreign ministry called again on Friday for a ceasefire and urged that the Strait of Hormuz be reopened "as soon as possible."
The issue is particularly significant for China, with nearly half of its crude oil imports passing through the strategic waterway.
Still, many in Beijing reportedly view the Iran crisis as outside China’s direct responsibility, raising questions over how far Xi is willing to cooperate with Washington on the issue.
Meanwhile, tensions around the strait continued to escalate as one ship anchored near the United Arab Emirates was seized and taken toward Iran on Thursday, while another cargo vessel near Oman sank following an attack.

Although no group immediately claimed responsibility, the incidents came as Iranian officials reiterated Tehran’s authority over the waterway and asserted its right to seize oil tankers linked to the United States.

Welcome to Within The Frame, where we bring the most pressing issues across the globe into focus. I'm Kim Mok-yeon.

At the same time, markets are responding to hopes of easing tensions.
Wall Street rallied after the summit, while Korea’s KOSPI surged past the 8,000 mark for the first time ever.

So, has this summit helped lower global economic uncertainty?

For a deeper discussion on this, we connect to Hwagyun Kim, a professor of banking and finance at Texas A&M University, Mays Business School. Welcome.


Also joining us is Sung Soo Eric Kim, founder & CEO of Datacrunch Global, and an adjunct professor at Yonsei Graduate School of Business. Good to see you. 
 

1. To begin with, the U.S. and China discussed trade imbalances and high-tech supply chains during their leaders' summit on the 14th.
From an economic standpoint, how would you assess the summit overall so far?


2. And the New York Times described the core agenda of the talks as the U.S. pushing its so-called “5Bs” while China focused on “3Ts.”
What does that tell us about the nature of these negotiations?


3. And several major U.S. tech CEOs, including Jensen Huang, Elon Musk and Tim Cook, joined the delegation.
What impact did that business delegation have?
And are these talks now expanding beyond trade into a broader battle over AI leadership?


4. Now, discussions over Nvidia’s H200 chips once again put AI chip export controls in focus.
After this summit, where do you see U.S.-China tech restrictions heading? Is there any room for easing them?


5. (Sung Soo) And what could this summit mean for Korean chipmakers like Samsung Electronics and SK hynix?
As supply chains continue to shift, what strategy should Korean companies be considering?


6. Meanwhile, China has been pressuring the U.S. through rare earth export controls.
Could this summit become a turning point in easing supply chain risks?


7. And just before the summit, there were signs of easing tensions in the energy sector, including reports of resumed U.S. LNG exports to China.
How much could this help stabilize raw material prices and inflation?


8. Now, hopes for tariff relief and easing supply chain tensions boosted Wall Street after the summit, while the KOSPI also crossed the 8,000 mark for the first time then pulled back. 
Against that backdrop, what impact could this summit have on global market volatility going forward?


9. And finally, where do you see the next battleground in the U.S.-China tech rivalry?

Debris from the unidentified aerial vehicle that struck a Korean-operated vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, has arrived in Seoul for detailed forensic analysis.
The foreign ministry said Friday that the fragments were transported by air on Thursday following consultations with United Arab Emirates authorities.
The debris includes engine parts collected from the scene of the attack last week on HMM Namu, moored in waters off the UAE.
A government investigation team examined the wreckage in Dubai, before it was stored at the South Korean Embassy in the UAE.
Officials say specialised agencies in Seoul will now carry out a detailed analysis, to help determine the type of UAV used in the strike.

snippet.title: Official candidate registration closes with last-minute merger agreements
snippet.description:
6•3 지선 후보등록 오늘 마감 민주•진보, 전격 합의하여 내주 울산 후보단일화

The two-day official candidate registration for the local elections ended today at 6 PM with last-minute variables, including candidate mergers appearing between the ruling Democratic Party and the Progressive Party in the city of Ulsan. 
Our political correspondent Ahn Sung-jin has the details.

Ahead of the June 3rd local elections, official candidate registration has wrapped up, setting the stage for intensified campaigning in several key battlegrounds across the country. 
The National Election Commission accepted registrations over two days ---May 14th and 15th ---and officials are expected to finalize ballot numbers for candidates based on parliamentary representation before official ballot printing on the 18th.
Candidate disclosures, including assets, criminal records, and tax payments, will be made public through the NEC election information system. 

Attention has centered on the southeastern city of Ulsan, where the ruling Democratic Party and the Progressive Party reached a last-minute agreement to unify their candidacies in a bid to challenge their conservative rival. 
Under the agreement, the two parties will select a single candidate for the mayor of Ulsan through public opinion polling. 
They also agreed to coordinate candidacies in five district-level county chief races as some candidates withdraw in favor of their allies, while others enter primary-style races to determine a unified nominee. 
This merger is expected to reshape the mayoral race in a traditionally conservative region, as recent opinion polls showed strong support for conservative candidates. 

The cooperation extends beyond Ulsan. 
The two parties also agreed to field a single candidate in the mayoral race for Yeonje-gu District in the southern port city of Busan. 
Similar consolidation deals have already emerged in several races nationwide, including district heads in Seoul, Daejeon, and Gyeongsangnam-do Province. 
Political parties across the spectrum are expected to continue negotiations ahead of two critical deadlines: candidates who withdraw by May 17th will have "withdrawn" marked beside their names on election day ballots, while those stepping down by the 28th, one day before early voting, will be identified as "withdrawn" on early voting ballots. 

The local elections are to elect 16 mayors and provincial governors, 227 county chiefs, more than 3,900 local council members, and 16 education superintendents, alongside 14 parliamentary seats through by-elections. 

Ahn Sung-jin, Arirang News.

localized.title: Official candidate registration closes with last-minute merger agreements
localized.description:
6•3 지선 후보등록 오늘 마감 민주•진보, 전격 합의하여 내주 울산 후보단일화

The two-day official candidate registration for the local elections ended today at 6 PM with last-minute variables, including candidate mergers appearing between the ruling Democratic Party and the Progressive Party in the city of Ulsan. 
Our political correspondent Ahn Sung-jin has the details.

Ahead of the June 3rd local elections, official candidate registration has wrapped up, setting the stage for intensified campaigning in several key battlegrounds across the country. 
The National Election Commission accepted registrations over two days ---May 14th and 15th ---and officials are expected to finalize ballot numbers for candidates based on parliamentary representation before official ballot printing on the 18th.
Candidate disclosures, including assets, criminal records, and tax payments, will be made public through the NEC election information system. 

Attention has centered on the southeastern city of Ulsan, where the ruling Democratic Party and the Progressive Party reached a last-minute agreement to unify their candidacies in a bid to challenge their conservative rival. 
Under the agreement, the two parties will select a single candidate for the mayor of Ulsan through public opinion polling. 
They also agreed to coordinate candidacies in five district-level county chief races as some candidates withdraw in favor of their allies, while others enter primary-style races to determine a unified nominee. 
This merger is expected to reshape the mayoral race in a traditionally conservative region, as recent opinion polls showed strong support for conservative candidates. 

The cooperation extends beyond Ulsan. 
The two parties also agreed to field a single candidate in the mayoral race for Yeonje-gu District in the southern port city of Busan. 
Similar consolidation deals have already emerged in several races nationwide, including district heads in Seoul, Daejeon, and Gyeongsangnam-do Province. 
Political parties across the spectrum are expected to continue negotiations ahead of two critical deadlines: candidates who withdraw by May 17th will have "withdrawn" marked beside their names on election day ballots, while those stepping down by the 28th, one day before early voting, will be identified as "withdrawn" on early voting ballots. 

The local elections are to elect 16 mayors and provincial governors, 227 county chiefs, more than 3,900 local council members, and 16 education superintendents, alongside 14 parliamentary seats through by-elections. 

Ahn Sung-jin, Arirang News.

snippet.description:

Across the western parts of the country today, it has already begun to feel like summer.
And starting tomorrow, that heat will spread nationwide, with most areas seeing daytime highs above 30 degrees Celsius through Sunday.
Clear skies tomorrow will bring strong sunshine throughout the day.
That means UV levels will be "very high" nationwide during the daytime.
Ozone concentrations are also expected to be "very bad" in the southern Gyeonggi-do Province, and most of the other areas will also experience "bad" levels. 
So, it’s best to limit outdoor activities during the hottest part of the day.
As for temperatures, Seoul will start the day at 18 degrees, Daejeon at 15, and Busan, 14 degrees.
Then by the afternoon, Seoul will get up to 31 degrees, Chuncheon and Daejeon, 31, and Daegu, up to even 33 degrees.
The early-season heat should start to ease by Wednesday next week as rain moves in.

snippet.title: KOSPI rallies past 8,000 before heavy selling pressure emerges
snippet.description:
코스피 사상 첫 8천 돌파 이후 하락 전환에 매도 사이드카까지

South Korea's benchmark KOSPI broke past the eight thousand mark for the first time during early trade on this Friday before closing its session lower on profit-taking.
Our economics correspondent Kim Jun-hong  has more.

Korea's benchmark KOSPI passed above the 8-thousand mark for the first time ever during trading on Friday.
 The index closed at 7-thousand-4-hundred-93-point18, down 6.12 percent from the previous session. 
 The move above 8-thousand came roughly ten minutes after the opening bell, just seven trading days after first breaking through the 7-thousand mark.
Yet sharp swings dominated trading throughout the day.
 The index seesawed between gains and losses before falling as much as seven percent from the previous session during trading, triggering a sell-side sidecar at one point.

Unlike the previous rally led by the country's chip giants, Friday's gains were powered by a wider group of market heavyweights.
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix both ended lower, while shares of LG Electronics and Hyundai Motor moved higher.

snippet.title: How Korea's cultural content could solve population decline in rural areas
snippet.description:
“지역 관광 해법 될까” 밀양 찾은 문체부 장관, 로컬관광 정책 점검

Culture Minister Chae Hwi-young  was in the city of Miryang  in Korea's Gyeongsangnam-do Province to learn firsthand about the impact of government programs to breathe new life into smaller cities through culture and tourism.
Our culture correspondent Park Kun-woo  was there.

Students sing and dance passionately during a performance inspired by "Miryang Arirang," a traditional folk song unique to the region.
In Miryang, a southeastern city grappling with population decline, these young students are also taking part in efforts to promote their hometown through local cultural performances.
This has been a big help, as the city's been designated as a "culture city" ---part of a governmental program aimed at revitalizing such regions through local cultural content.


"I feel like I should have visited much earlier. Local culture seems to be growing stronger on the foundations we've worked on. We'll continue listening to what support is needed and do our best moving forward."

During a two-day visit to the city, Culture Minister Chae Hwi-young also met with local residents to hear firsthand about the challenges they face.
Miryang has been one of the pioneer cities to apply the government-backed "half-cost travel" program, and officials say they've witnessed a boost in visitor numbers.
But local merchants are asking for more support.


"I hope the program can be promoted earlier and backed with a larger budget so more people can benefit from it. If the half-price travel program becomes more active, it will greatly help revitalize the regional economy."

Amid the shrinking population, people relocating to the countryside and setting up their own businesses is also becoming more noticeable in the city.
But some say support programs are sometimes unreachable.


"I'm in my 40s, and when it comes to support programs or opportunities to participate, I've become too old to qualify. In agriculture, people are considered young enough to earn support until 50, so I hope there can be broader support for people like us as well."


"It's inspiring to see the younger generation's efforts to rediscover strengths in places once weakened, and these efforts deserve continued support. More successful cases need to emerge so that others will also be inspired to follow the path."


"With more support from the culture ministry and continued efforts to further develop the region’s cultural content, the area is now looking to attract more visitors and boost regional growth.
Park Kun-woo, Arirang News, Miryang."

snippet.title: Korea's diplomacy in practice: dialogue with global youth, overseas Koreans protection
snippet.description:
"세계와 진정한 대화”로 실용외교 넓히는 한국.. 공공외교대사•재외국민보호 정부대표

The Lee administration's pragmatic diplomacy includes advancing bilateral interests with partners in the Global South.
This being said my colleague Oh Soo-young  reached out to a senior official at the Foreign Ministry here for a better understanding of these related efforts.
Do take a listen.

People and partnerships are at the heart of Seoul’s expanding diplomatic reach.
Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Lim Sang-woo is playing an active role in deepening ties across the Global South, while strengthening support for Koreans abroad.
Since taking office last December, Kenya and Madagascar were among his first overseas trips, ahead of a ministerial meeting involving 54 African countries next month.

“This is also in the context of our diplomacy that focuses more on strengthening our relationship with the Global South and of course in Africa is an integral part of the Global South.”

Global South outreach featured in President Lee Jae Myung’s summit last month with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, marking the first Korean state visit to India in eight years.
One crucial agreement supports Korean SMEs investing in India, an initiative Lim personally worked on during his posting in New Delhi.
His diplomacy went beyond official meetings.
From creating viral videos to volunteering as a guide at India’s National Museum, a first for a foreign diplomat.
His outreach now informs his role overseeing KOREAZ, the foreign ministry’s public diplomacy platform,.. supported by 20 Koreans and 20 foreign nationals representing 18 countries.

“We are committed to running this channel not as just a platform to showcase Korean culture but a channel where genuine dialogue takes place with our friends from all over the world."

But as Korea’s global reach expands, so does the responsibility of protecting some seven million overseas nationals, amid risks from armed conflict and natural disasters, to transnational crime.

“Our guiding principle has been to provide Koreans security protection that they would expect to have at home.
So in that way Koreans wherever they are in the world can feel secure and feel safe having this assurance that the government will be there to provide assistance if needed.”

Lim last week travelled to Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, where Seoul is working with local authorities to tackle online scam operations involving Koreans.

“The most critical tool we can use to combat transnational crime is real-time intelligence. There has to be a real-time sharing of intelligence amongst the law enforcement authorities, and there has to be swift and decisive action based on those real time intelligence.”

From serving in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and as Korea’s first resident ambassador to Madagascar, Lim has built relationships from the ground up, 
and responded to consular crises in times of conflict and pandemic.
Oh Soo-young, Arirang News.

Findings for the month of April by the Bank of Korea show export prices up and import prices down BUT officials remain on edge about the potential broader implications of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East.
Lee Eun-jin  has the latest.

South Korea's export prices surged in April, with the export price index marking 187-point-four-zero, up 7-point-1 percent from the previous month. 
This, according to data from the Bank of Korea on Friday, marks the tenth consecutive month of growth, led by the manufacturing sector, including computer, electronic, and optical equipment, and largely attributed to the sharp increase in semiconductor prices.
Central bank data also shows import prices fell 2-point-3 percent on-month in April, marking the first on-month drop in 10 months.
South Korea relies heavily on energy imports.
The decline came as the price of Dubai Crude -South Korea's benchmark - fell 17-point-8 percent on-month to 105 U.S. dollars and 7 cents per barrel, affected by the U.S. and Iran agreeing to a ceasefire on April 7th.
However, prolonged geopolitical tensions in the region continue to pose upward risks for future raw material supplies.
Prices of raw materials fell 9-point-7 percent in April from a month earlier, while intermediate goods rose 2-point-1 percent.
Despite these uncertainties, the country's net barter terms of trade index improved, jumping 14-point-3 percent on-year.

to minimize the economic hardships faced by the people, as it also works to promptly implement supportive measures through a supplementary budget.

snippet.title: Busan Haeundae Beach transforms into a golden art gallery
snippet.description:
해운대가 금빛의 갤러리로 변하는 순간: 2026 모래축제 개막

MEANWHILE in the southern port city of Busan starting today.
Haeundae Beach is hosting its annual Sand Festival and this year about a dozen international artists have on display a collection of carefully crafted sculptures that share the story of Busan then and now.
Our culture correspondent Chung Hye-lim  files this report.

Here in the port city of Busan, Haeundae Beach has been transformed into a massive outdoor gallery for the 21st annual Sand Festival. 
This year, the shores are playing host to "A Journey through Busan’s History by Sand," featuring 17 monumental works that bridge the city’s past with its ambitious future.
Eleven world-class artists from five countries have spent weeks sculpting everything from Busan’s historic spots, to its modern identity as a hub for cinema and its love for baseball.

“We wanted to capture the entire panoramic view of Busan within a single work. We use the natural sand right here from Haeundae Beach. We compress the sand using molds and then carve from the very top down to the bottom. Other sculptors were actually shocked by the level of detail—specifically how we hand-carved every single window in the buildings by hand.”


"This piece portrays Busan during the Korean War, where it served as a temporary capital and embraced countless refugees.
Pieces like this represent the city's history through sand, who truly witnessed it all."

For the thousands of visitors, the scale of the work is astonishing.

“I'm here on a school field trip. It's so cool, and the sculptors must have put in so much care. It looks like it would have taken a long time to make."

“So we’re here in Busan for the day, we wanted to come and visit the beach. () ( ) They’re cool, I like them. () The biggest one is their favorite.”

“We came to have lunch nearby and heard about the sand festival, so we stopped by. I saw the Train to Busan piece, and it’s much more detailed than I expected—you can even recognize the actors, which was really fun."

The festival offers more than just sightseeing. 
Thrill-seekers can hit the dunes for sandboarding, while families can engage in water gun battles or learn the secrets of sand sculpting themselves.
The main festivities and interactive programs run through May 18th. 
However, the 17 masterpieces will remain on display for the public to enjoy until June 14th.
Chung Hye-lim, Arirang News, Busan.

snippet.title: [Weather] Summer heat continues through the weekend with high UV, ozone levels
snippet.description:
주말도 여름 더위, 자외선•오존 강해

It was another hot day today, and daytime highs above 30 degrees Celsius are expected to continue through the weekend.
For now, inland regions will continue to see big day-to-night temperature swings of around 15 degrees Celsius in many areas.
So short sleeves will be just fine during the day this weekend, but it’s still a good idea to keep a light jacket handy for cooler mornings and evenings.
Clear skies tomorrow will bring strong sunshine throughout the day.
That means UV levels will be "very high" nationwide during the daytime.
Ozone concentrations are also expected to be "bad" in the capital area, Chungcheong-do, and Jeollabuk-do provinces. 
So it’s best to limit outdoor activities during the hottest part of the day.
As for temperatures, Seoul will start the day at 18 degrees, Daejeon, 15, and Busan, 14 degrees. 
Then by the afternoon, Seoul will get up to 31 degrees, Chuncheon and Daejeon, 31, and Daegu, up to even 33 degrees. 
The early-season heat should finally back off around Wednesday next week, as rain moves into the country.

snippet.title: Trump and Xi wrap up "milestone" Beijing summit with rare garden tour
snippet.description:
트럼프•시진핑 ‘중난하이 산책’으로 방중 마무리 “환상적인 무역 합의 이뤄냈다”

U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping end their latest encounter in Beijing with more talks over tea today and an earlier invitation by the former to the latter for another summit in September this time at the White House.
Our Kim Do-yeon  reports.
 
The summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping ended on Friday with a symbolic gesture at the walled-off Zhongnanhai complex.
The two had lunch and tea at the special venue and President Xi offered a rare glimpse into the private imperial gardens—a gesture typically reserved for China’s closest allies.

"Can I ask the President, with other dignitaries from other countries, Presidents or Prime Ministers, does he bring them here?"

"Very few. We usually don’t hold diplomatic events here. Even after we started having some, it’s still extremely rare. For example: Putin."

"Good, I like it."

Both leaders characterized the three-day visit as a fundamental shift in bilateral ties. 
President Trump praised the personal rapport he has built with his counterpart over the last decade, suggesting their chemistry has allowed them to bypass traditional diplomatic gridlock.

"And we’ve settled a lot of different problems that other people wouldn’t have been able to settle, and the relationship is a very strong one."

"So far, we have established a new bilateral relationship, or rather a constructive relationship of strategic stability. This could be described as a milestone visit."

On the economic front, President Trump indicated that he is returning to Washington with significant progress toward "fantastic trade deals." 
In an interview with Fox News, Trump described President Xi as "all business," noting a pragmatic commitment to economic coordination.
The U.S. leader said China has committed to major purchases of American goods, including a large order of Boeing aircraft and a significant increase in imports of U.S. agricultural products, specifically soybeans while gradually opening parts of its economy to U.S. businesses.
To manage these ongoing economic ties, the two sides have agreed to establish a new "Board of Trade" to handle disputes without immediately resorting to new tariffs.
However no joint statement or declaration was adopted by the two leaders for this trip. 
The two will meet again this year as on Thursday Trump invited Xi to the U.S. in September. 
Kim Do-yeon, Arirang News.

U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping end their latest encounter in Beijing with more talks over tea today and an earlier invitation by the former to the latter for another summit in September this time at the White House.
Our Kim Do-yeon  reports.
 
The summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping ended on Friday with a symbolic gesture at the walled-off Zhongnanhai complex.
The two had lunch and tea at the special venue and President Xi offered a rare glimpse into the private imperial gardens—a gesture typically reserved for China’s closest allies.

"Can I ask the President, with other dignitaries from other countries, Presidents or Prime Ministers, does he bring them here?"

"Very few. We usually don’t hold diplomatic events here. Even after we started having some, it’s still extremely rare. For example: Putin."

"Good, I like it."

Both leaders characterized the three-day visit as a fundamental shift in bilateral ties. 
President Trump praised the personal rapport he has built with his counterpart over the last decade, suggesting their chemistry has allowed them to bypass traditional diplomatic gridlock.

"And we’ve settled a lot of different problems that other people wouldn’t have been able to settle, and the relationship is a very strong one."

"So far, we have established a new bilateral relationship, or rather a constructive relationship of strategic stability. This could be described as a milestone visit."

On the economic front, President Trump indicated that he is returning to Washington with significant progress toward "fantastic trade deals." 
In an interview with Fox News, Trump described President Xi as "all business," noting a pragmatic commitment to economic coordination.

snippet.title: [K-Enter] BTS to perform at 2026 FIFA World Cup final halftime show
snippet.description:
BTS, 북중미 월드컵 결승전 하프타임쇼 선다

Walter, earlier this week we talked about BLACKPINK'S Lisa doing one of the opening performances for this year's FIFA World Cup, but it looks like she won't be the only K-pop artist to perform at the World Cup, right?

 
Indeed Soa, BTS will appear as a co-headliner at the halftime show of the 2026 FIFA World Cup final. Madonna and Shakira will also be a part of the halftime show. This is the first time a halftime show will be held during a FIFA World Cup final.

The half time show is expected to raise awareness for the “FIFA Global Citizen Education Fund”, which aims to expand access to quality education and sports programs for children. BTS has had a long partnership with Global Citizen, having appeared at “Global Citizen Live” in 2021, while member Jungkook  took the stage at the “Global Citizen Festival” in 2023.

BTS are currently on their “ARIRANG” world tour with upcoming performances at Stanford Stadium in California on May 16, 17 and 20, becoming the first Korean artist to hold a concert at the venue. 


Next up some exciting news for KPop Demon Hunters fans.


Netflix announced on Thursday through its official Tudum platform that it is teaming up with live entertainment company AEG Presents, to create a worldwide tour based on "KPop Demon Hunters". Netflix described the project as an immersive live event that will transform the universe of “KPop Demon Hunters” into a spectacular real-world experience and are bringing the magic of the Honmoon  to venues around the world. In KPop Demon Hunters, the Honmoon , also known as the “Soul Gate,” is a mystical barrier created to protect the human world from demonic forces.
The official lineup for the performances is not confirmed but fans are especially eager to see whether artists like EJAE , Audrey Nuna, and REI AMI, who were the singing voices for HUNTR/X, perform with the demon boy group Saja Boys. Additional details, including tour dates and host cities, are scheduled to be revealed later this year.


Last but not least, let's talk about a boy group that's making milestones in Japan. 


According to the Recording Industry Association of Japan on Friday, Tomorrow X Together’s  eighth mini album, “When The Wind Briefly Stopped In the Thorn Bush,” exceeded 250-thousand cumulative shipments in Japan as of April, securing a Platinum certification under the organisation’s Gold Disc system.

The latest achievement brings the group’s total number of Gold Disc-certified releases in Japan to 16. The Association grants Gold certification for shipments exceeding 100,000 copies, Platinum for 250,000, Double Platinum for 500,000, Triple Platinum for 750,000.

The mini album also maintained strong momentum on Oricon’s charts, reaching No. 1 on the Weekly Combined Album Ranking, Weekly Album Ranking, and Weekly Western Music Album Ranking. Notably, it became the group’s 14th chart-topper on the Weekly Combined Album Ranking, tying the all-time record for the most No. 1 albums among both domestic Japanese and international artists.

South Korea’s port city of Busan has kicked off its renowned Sand Festival.
Famous for sand sculptures by artists from around the world, the festival is one of Busan’s main tourist attractions.
To tell us more, we have our culture correspondent,  Chung Hye-lim at Haeundae Beach.
Hye-lim, how’s it looking right now?
Good afternoon Eunji, I’m standing in front of the festival’s main sand sculpture.
It is warm and sunny, and the weather really reflects the hot atmosphere right now, with hundreds of visitors already here on the first day of the 2026 Haeundae Sand Festival.
This year’s theme is “A Journey through Busan’s History by Sand,” and the main sculpture features some famous Busan spots including LCT and Nurimaru APEC House.
Right now, seventeen massive sculptures have transformed the beach into a living history book.
On Thursday, I got to speak with one of the main sculptors of the iconic main piece.

“We wanted to capture the entire panoramic view of Busan within a single work. We use the natural sand right here from Haeundae Beach. We compress the sand using molds and then carve from the very top down to the bottom. Other sculptors were actually shocked by the level of detail—specifically how we hand-carved every single window in the buildings by hand.”

That’s fascinating to hear, Hye-lim. So what are visitors saying about the festival, and are there other activities they can get involved in?

Back to you, Eunji.

snippet.title: Korea's diplomacy in practice: dialogue with global youth, overseas Koreans protection
snippet.description:
"세계와 진정한 대화”로 실용외교 넓히는 한국.. 공공외교대사•재외국민보호 정부대표

As Seoul looks to deepen its strategic partnerships, as emphasised by the Foreign Minister on Thursday,.. a senior diplomat spoke with Arirang to highlight how pragmatic diplomacy is unfolding in practice.
Oh Soo-young has more.

People and partnerships are at the heart of Seoul’s expanding diplomatic reach.
Deputy Minister for Public Diplomacy Lim Sang-woo is playing an active role in deepening ties across the Global South, while strengthening support for Koreans abroad.
Since taking office last December, Kenya and Madagascar were among his first overseas trips, ahead of a ministerial meeting involving 54 African countries next month.

“This is also in the context of our diplomacy that focuses more on strengthening our relationship with the Global South and of course in Africa is an integral part of the Global South.”

Global South outreach featured in President Lee Jae Myung’s summit last month with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, marking the first Korean state visit to India in eight years.

“Both leaders demonstrated their strong resolve to take our Korea-India relations to the next level especially with an emphasis on strengthening collaboration in key strategic industries such as semiconductors, shipbuilding and AI. We also had the 15 MOUs signed on that occasion and we agreed to establish a ministerial-level platform to discuss these very important areas.”

One crucial agreement supports Korean SMEs investing in India, an initiative Lim personally worked on during his posting in New Delhi.
His diplomacy went beyond official meetings.
From creating viral videos to volunteering as a guide at India’s National Museum, a first for a foreign diplomat.

His outreach now informs his role overseeing KOREAZ, the foreign ministry’s public diplomacy platform,.. supported by 20 Koreans and 20 foreign nationals representing 18 countries.

“We are committed to running this channel not as just a platform to showcase Korean culture but a channel where genuine dialogue takes place with our friends from all over the world. This year we’ve actually launched a campaign called 'the Youthful Tomorrow,' where it’s all about youth empowerment and how the youth can get together to map out the future."

But as Korea’s global reach expands, so does the responsibility of protecting some seven million overseas nationals, amid risks from armed conflict and natural disasters, to transnational crime.

“Our guiding principle has been to provide Koreans security protection that they would expect to have at home.
So in that way Koreans wherever they are in the world can feel secure and feel safe having this assurance that the government will be there to provide assistance if needed.”

Lim last week travelled to Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, where Seoul is working with local authorities to tackle online scam operations involving Koreans.

“The most critical tool we can use to combat transnational crime is real-time intelligence. There has to be a real-time sharing of intelligence amongst the law enforcement authorities, and there has to be swift and decisive action based on those real time intelligence.”

From serving in the Democratic Republic of Congo, and as Korea’s first resident ambassador to Madagascar, Lim has built relationships from the ground up, and responded to consular crises in times of conflict and pandemic.
Oh Soo-young, Arirang News.

snippet.title: CIA director meets with top Cuban officials in Havana amid rising fuel crisis
snippet.description:
미 CIA 국장 쿠바 전격 방문 및 고위급 회담 개최

This is the WORLD NOW, bringing you everything you need to know from around the globe.
CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Havana on Thursday for a rare face-to-face meeting with Cuban interior ministry officials.This comes as fuel shortages caused in part by a U.S. blockade push the island into rolling blackouts, sparking widespread protests in the capital. Cuba said both sides expressed interest in law enforcement cooperation and that Cuban officials stressed the island poses no threat to U.S. national security. Ratcliffe's visit follows Trump’s warning earlier this year that Cuba was next after U.S. forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January.
Russian attacks destroyed a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv on Thursday, killing nine people including a 12-year-old girl, in the third consecutive day of massive strikes on Ukraine. More than twenty residents are still missing. Ukraine’s air force called it the largest aerial assault since Russia’s full-scale invasion began, with more than one-thousand-five-hundred-sixty drones fired at Ukrainian population centers since Wednesday. Some one-hundred-eighty sites across the country were damaged including over fifty residential buildings.
Ukrainian officials called on Trump and Xi Jinping, meeting in Beijing, to use their leverage to pressure Putin to stop the attacks.
Closing arguments wrapped up on Thursday in Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI.
Musk’s lawyers called OpenAI CEO Sam Altman "a liar" and OpenAI’s lawyers accused Musk of selective amnesia and said he simply wanted to control the company himself.
Musk is seeking one hundred fifty billion dollars in damages and wants Altman removed.
He alleges OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit mission by accepting tens of billions from Microsoft. OpenAI argues that Musk knew about its plans years before filing suit and waited too long to take legal action. A verdict could come as early as next week.
Egypt's Luxor Museum on Thursday displayed for the first time a plaster wall from King Tutankhamun’s tomb.
It is the only surviving artifact of its kind in the world that hasn't been seen by the public, and is being displayed more than a century after the tomb’s discovery in 1922.
The wall bears the seals of Tutankhamun and the guards who protected his tomb. Two newly restored ancient tombs from Egypt’s eighteenth dynasty were also unveiled, containing scenes of daily life including agriculture, pottery, wine production and funerary rituals.

snippet.title: Trump, Xi agree on Iran issues during summit in Beijing: White House
snippet.description:
'이란핵 불용•호르무즈 개방' 일치 中 역할할진 미지수

U.S. President Donald Trump says he reached a key understanding with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz during summit talks in Beijing.
Trump also claimed Xi offered to help negotiate an end to the conflict and pledged that China would not provide military equipment to Tehran.
Lee Seung-jae has more.

U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed during summit talks in Beijing that Iran must never obtain nuclear weapons and that the Strait of Hormuz should remain open, in a development that could help revive stalled U.S.-Iran peace negotiations.
According to the White House on Thursday, both leaders agreed on the importance of keeping the strategically vital shipping route open to protect global energy supplies. 
Washington also stated that Xi opposed any militarization of the strait and expressed interest in increasing U.S. crude oil purchases.
The agreement reflects one of Trump’s key demands for ending the conflict in the Middle East. 
Ahead of the summit, U.S. officials had urged China to use its influence over Tehran to help ease tensions in the Gulf region.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said China has a strong interest in resolving the crisis because it relies heavily on energy shipments passing through the Strait of Hormuz. 
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also said Beijing was expected to engage figures close to Iran’s leadership quietly.
China, however, struck a noticeably more cautious tone after the talks. 
Beijing confirmed Middle East issues were discussed, but did not specifically mention the White House claim that both sides agreed Iran should never possess nuclear weapons. 
Analysts say China appears reluctant to fully align with Washington’s approach, as it seeks to preserve leverage over Iran while protecting its own strategic interests in the region.
Following the summit, Trump told Fox News that Xi had also offered to help negotiate an end to the war and support efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to global shipping. 
Trump said Xi expressed a willingness to play a constructive role in helping resolve the conflict and stabilize shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
The U.S. president also claimed Xi assured him China would not provide military equipment to Iran, although questions remain over Beijing’s broader economic and strategic ties with Tehran.
Lee Seung-jae, Arirang News.

snippet.title: Export price index up as global chip prices rise
snippet.description:
반도체 가격 상승에 4월 수출물가 7.1%↑ 수입물가는 2.3%↓

South Korea's export prices surged in April, driven by sharp increases in semiconductor prices.
According to the Bank of Korea on Friday, the export price index for April stood at 187-point-40, up 7-point-1 percent from the previous month to mark its tenth consecutive month of growth.
This growth was largely led by the manufacturing sector, specifically computer, electronic, and optical equipment. 
The import price index fell 2-point-3 percent from the previous month as global oil prices eased from earlier spikes triggered by the Middle East conflict. 
However, prolonged geopolitical tensions in the region continue to pose upward risks for future raw material supplies.
Despite these uncertainties, the country's net barter terms of trade index improved, jumping 14-point-3 percent on-year.

코스피, 장중 8000선 돌파 ‘8천피’ 시대 열었다

Korea's benchmark KOSPI surpassed the 8-thousand mark for the first time ever during intraday trading on Friday.
The index opened at 7-thousand-9-hundred-51-point-75, down 0-point-37 percent from the previous close.
Those losses soon reversed course for a climb above the 8-thousand level inside just thirteen minutes of trading.
The record came only seven trading days after the benchmark first broke the 7-thousand mark.
The KOSPI closed on Thursday at a new all-time high, only nineteen points off the 8-thousand level.

snippet.title: CIA director meets with top Cuban officials in Havana amid fuel crisis
snippet.description:

CIA Director John Ratcliffe traveled to Havana on Thursday for a rare face-to-face meeting with Cuban interior ministry officials.
This comes as fuel shortages caused in part by a U.S. blockade push the island into rolling blackouts, sparking widespread protests in the capital.
Cuba said both sides expressed interest in law enforcement cooperation and that Cuban officials stressed the island poses no threat to U.S. national security. Ratcliffe's visit follows Trump’s warning earlier this year that Cuba was next after U.S. forces captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January.

snippet.title: Russian missile strike destroys Kyiv apartment building leaving nine dead
snippet.description:

Russian attacks destroyed a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv on Thursday, killing nine people including a 12-year-old girl, in the third consecutive day of massive strikes on Ukraine.
More than twenty residents are still missing. Ukraine’s air force called it the largest aerial assault since Russia’s full-scale invasion began, with more than one-thousand-five-hundred-sixty drones fired at Ukrainian population centers since Wednesday. Some one-hundred-eighty sites across the country were damaged including over fifty residential buildings.
Ukrainian officials called on Trump and Xi Jinping, meeting in Beijing, to use their leverage to pressure Putin to stop the attacks.

snippet.title: Closing arguments begin in Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman
snippet.description:
일론 머스크와 오픈AI 법정 공방 최종 변론 진행

Closing arguments wrapped up on Thursday in Elon Musk’s lawsuit against OpenAI.
Musk’s lawyers called OpenAI CEO Sam Altman "a liar" and OpenAI’s lawyers accused Musk of selective amnesia and said he simply wanted to control the company himself.
Musk is seeking one hundred fifty billion dollars in damages and wants Altman removed. 
He alleges OpenAI betrayed its nonprofit mission by accepting tens of billions from Microsoft. OpenAI argues that Musk knew about its plans years before filing suit and waited too long to take legal action. A verdict could come as early as next week.

snippet.title: Egypt displays Tutankhamun tomb artifact and restored New Kingdom tombs
snippet.description:
이집트 투탕카멘 유물 공개 및 신왕국 시대 무덤 복원 완료

Egypt's Luxor Museum on Thursday displayed for the first time a plaster wall from King Tutankhamun’s tomb.
It is the only surviving artifact of its kind in the world that hasn't been seen by the public, and is being displayed more than a century after the tomb’s discovery in 1922.
The wall bears the seals of Tutankhamun and the guards who protected his tomb. Two newly restored ancient tombs from Egypt’s eighteenth dynasty were also unveiled, containing scenes of daily life including agriculture, pottery, wine production and funerary rituals.

This unusual heat, hovering nearly 10 degrees higher than norms, will continue through the weekend under dazzling sunshine, plan accordingly for any outdoor activities. 
Skies will stay mostly sunny nationwide today, and strong sunshine will push UV levels very high during the afternoon. Have your sun protection items ready. 
And this afternoon, Seoul gets up to sizzling 32 degrees Celsius, Gwangju at 30 degrees, Busan and Jeju should be more comfortable at 24 degrees. 
Looking ahead next week, heat relief is expected next Wednesday, when rain moves in nationwide and helps cool temperatures back down to near seasonal norms.

snippet.title: Trump, Xi summit wraps on Friday with no practical agreements made yet
snippet.description:
트럼프•시진핑 협력 의지 확인 무역위원회 신설에도 ‘대타협’은 없어

We begin today in Beijing,.. where U.S. President Donald Trump concludes his state visit today.
Despite the presence of American tech executives signaling a sharp focus on economic competition, the summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping has yielded no sweeping structural trade agreements.
Our Kim Do-yeon reports.

U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are entering the final hours of Trump's high-stakes state visit to Beijing. 
Discussions have so far yielded no practical agreements or breakthroughs on core structural issues, instead, the focus has remained on personal diplomacy and the management of a competitive relationship.
Cooperation was emphasized during a state banquet on Thursday, both through President Trump's invitation to the Chinese leader to visit Washington later this year and President Xi's reply.

"Thank you again, President Xi, for this beautiful welcome. And tonight, it is my honor to extend an invitation to you and Madam Peng to visit us at the White House this September twenty-fourth. And we look forward to it."

"The people of China and the United States are both great peoples. The goals of realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can fully proceed in parallel without contradiction. They can mutually reinforce each other and benefit the world."

However, the rhetoric has not translated into policy shifts, with friction remaining over tech export controls and industrial subsidies.
Furthermore, the two sides have yet to reach an agreement regarding Taiwan, leaving the most sensitive point of regional tension unresolved.
Before the official conclusion of the state visit, the two leaders are scheduled to meet at the Zhongnanhai compound for tea and a working lunch. 
This is expected to be followed by a highly publicized stroll, providing one last opportunity for dialogue before President Trump departs the Chinese capital.
Kim Do-yeon, Arirang News.

snippet.title: Gov't sees low possibility of non-Iranian actor being behind attack on HMM Namu
snippet.description:
조현, "나무호 공격, 어떤 경우에도 정당화될 수 없어," 고위당국자 "이란 이외 주체가 공격했을 가능성 낮아"

South Korea believes that there is little possibility of a non-Iranian actor being behind the attack on the HMM Namu in the Strait of Hormuz on May 4th.
Foreign Minister Cho Hyun later added that attacks on Korea's civilian vessels can never be justified.
Cha Yun-kyung reports.

The government believes that Iran was behind the attack on a South Korean-operated vessel, the HMM Namu, in the Strait of Hormuz on May 4th.
A senior official said Thursday that the government is gathering evidence related to the strike on the cargo vessel.
He noted that "the possibility of another actor besides Iran cannot be ruled out, however, common sense suggests this is unlikely since there were no pirates nearby."
The official cautioned that Seoul has not yet formally confirmed the result yet, emphasizing that any conclusion regarding Iranian involvement would depend on the outcome of an ongoing probe, assisted by the U.S.

Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Thursday that "attacks on civilian vessels, including the HMM Namu, can never be justified or tolerated under any circumstances."
Cho added that "an additional government-level investigation into the attack on the HMM Namu will be conducted." He said "necessary response measures will be taken accordingly," continuing that the government will make an effort to cooperate with related countries amid heightened geopolitical uncertainties.

The Ministry of National Defense announced Thursday that it had sent a technical analysis team to Dubai to determine the cause and conduct a scientific analysis of the attack on the HMM Namu.
The ministry said, "It will support the activities of the government joint response team by conducting a thorough on-site investigation, analyzing evidence to confirm the exact facts." 

The ministry added that "the number of personnel dispatched and details of their activities would not be disclosed to ensure smooth investigative activities."

Cha Yun-kyung, Arirang News.

snippet.title: [Econ & Biz] With memory chip supercycle, Korea's fiscal health improves
snippet.description:
계속 되는 반도체 수출 호조… 나라살림 적자에도 벌써 도움

Korea's economy is seeing a massive boost, driven largely by a historic boom in the technology sector. 
Not only have information and communication technology exports reached an all-time high, but this semiconductor supercycle is also helping to rapidly improve the government's fiscal health. 
Joining us in the studio to break down these numbers and the broader implications is our Business and Economy correspondent Kim Do-yeon. Welcome.

Good to be here.

Let's start with the export data. April was a milestone month for the tech sector. Walk us through the latest figures.

That's right ICT exports logged their highest growth rate in history last month. 
Export volume reached 42.71 billion U.S. dollars, which is a 125.9 percent surge compared to the same month last year. 
This marks the first time ICT exports have surpassed the 40-billion-dollar mark for two consecutive months. 
The semiconductor sector is doing the heavy lifting, skyrocketing 173.3 percent on-year.
The global tech industry is racing to build artificial intelligence infrastructure, creating a severe bottleneck for high-performance memory chips. 
Here is what one industry expert had to say about this momentum.

"The reason our ICT exports are hitting all-time highs right now is the supply shortage in memory chip exports, which is driving prices incredibly high. Because of this, it's very likely we will break records again next month."

And we are already seeing this spill over into the computer and peripheral devices sector, which saw a staggering 430 percent export increase, heavily influenced by the AI-driven demand for solid-state drives.

It is interesting how this industrial boom is translating directly into the national treasury. The government's first-quarter fiscal data released today shows a significantly narrowed deficit.

According to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the managed fiscal balance—which indicates the government's actual fiscal state—posted a deficit of 39.6 trillion won in the first quarter. 
While still a deficit, this is an improvement of 21.7 trillion won compared to a year ago, making it the narrowest first-quarter deficit in six years.
This was driven by a massive increase in total revenue, which reached 188.8 trillion won. 
A closer look reveals that income tax revenue rose by 4.7 trillion won, fueled directly by increased performance bonuses for employees at semiconductor giants like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix along with other industries and government policies. 
But bonuses are important because a big portion of the bonuses are taxed. 
However, experts point out that relying so heavily on just one sector creates a dangerous optical illusion for the broader economy. Take a listen.

"Because of companies in a small number of industries, it looks like our economy is doing well and recovering, but in some ways, this is a severe polarization. The industries that are struggling are simply continuing to struggle. So, while we can't say it's strictly just semiconductors, it is true that this is limited to a few industries and a few companies."

Essentially, while the headline numbers and government coffers look phenomenal thanks to chips, other sectors of the domestic economy are still struggling, meaning the wealth is not trickling down evenly.

You mentioned the performance bonuses at semiconductor companies boosting national tax revenues. But ironically, those same bonuses are currently the source of a major dispute within Samsung Electronics. What is the latest on the strike concerns?

The situation at Samsung is reaching a critical point as the gap between labor and management remains wide.
The union is specifically demanding that the company institutionalize a fixed performance bonus of 15 percent of its operating profit for the semiconductor division. 
They are also calling for the removal of the current cap on bonuses, which is currently set at 50 percent of an employee's annual salary.
Management, however, is standing firm on maintaining its existing incentive system based on economic value added, though it has proposed additional special rewards for the semiconductor unit.
Following the breakdown of negotiations early Wednesday, May 13th, the union has set a firm deadline. 
They are demanding a response by 10 AM tomorrow, May 15th...

Korea's economy is seeing a massive boost, driven largely by a historic boom in the technology sector. 
Not only have information and communication technology exports reached an all-time high, but this semiconductor supercycle is also helping to rapidly improve the government's fiscal health. 
Joining us in the studio to break down these numbers and the broader implications is our Business and Economy correspondent Kim Do-yeon. Welcome.

Good to be here.

Let's start with the export data. April was a milestone month for the tech sector. Walk us through the latest figures.

That's right ICT exports logged their highest growth rate in history last month. 
Export volume reached 42.71 billion U.S. dollars, which is a 125.9 percent surge compared to the same month last year. 
This marks the first time ICT exports have surpassed the 40-billion-dollar mark for two consecutive months. 
The semiconductor sector is doing the heavy lifting, skyrocketing 173.3 percent on-year.
The global tech industry is racing to build artificial intelligence infrastructure, creating a severe bottleneck for high-performance memory chips. 
Here is what one industry expert had to say about this momentum.

"The reason our ICT exports are hitting all-time highs right now is the supply shortage in memory chip exports, which is driving prices incredibly high. Because of this, it's very likely we will break records again next month."

And we are already seeing this spill over into the computer and peripheral devices sector, which saw a staggering 430 percent export increase, heavily influenced by the AI-driven demand for solid-state drives.

It is interesting how this industrial boom is translating directly into the national treasury. The government's first-quarter fiscal data released today shows a significantly narrowed deficit.

According to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the managed fiscal balance—which indicates the government's actual fiscal state—posted a deficit of 39.6 trillion won in the first quarter. 
While still a deficit, this is an improvement of 21.7 trillion won compared to a year ago, making it the narrowest first-quarter deficit in six years.
This was driven by a massive increase in total revenue, which reached 188.8 trillion won. 
A closer look reveals that income tax revenue rose by 4.7 trillion won, fueled directly by increased performance bonuses for employees at semiconductor giants like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix along with other industries and government policies. 
But bonuses are important because a big portion of the bonuses are taxed. 
However, experts point out that relying so heavily on just one sector creates a dangerous optical illusion for the broader economy. Take a listen.

"Because of companies in a small number of industries, it looks like our economy is doing well and recovering, but in some ways, this is a severe polarization. The industries that are struggling are simply continuing to struggle. So, while we can't say it's strictly just semiconductors, it is true that this is limited to a few industries and a few companies."

Essentially, while the headline numbers and government coffers look phenomenal thanks to chips, other sectors of the domestic economy are still struggling, meaning the wealth is not trickling down evenly.

You mentioned the performance bonuses at semiconductor companies boosting national tax revenues. But ironically, those same bonuses are currently the source of a major dispute within Samsung Electronics. What is the latest on the strike concerns?

The situation at Samsung is reaching a critical point as the gap between labor and management remains wide.
The union is specifically demanding that the company institutionalize a fixed performance bonus of 15 percent of its operating profit for the semiconductor division. 
They are also calling for the removal of the current cap on bonuses, which is currently set at 50 percent of an employee's annual salary.
Management, however, is standing firm on maintaining its existing incentive system based on economic value added, though it has proposed additional special rewards for the semiconductor unit.
Following the breakdown of negotiations early Wednesday, May 13th, the union has set a firm deadline. 
They are demanding a response by 10 AM tomorrow, May 15th...
